articleTitle: Measurements to 320 GHz of millimetre-wave waveguide components made by high precision and economic micro-machining techniques
publicationTitle: 2003 High Frequency Postgraduate Student Colloquium (Cat. No.03TH8707)
abstract: A new technique for the fabrication and integration of various waveguide components together with an integrated E-plane circuit to form a compact millimetre-wave subcomponent has been produced. These waveguide components were fabricated in two halves using SU-8 such that the circuits can be placed in the E-plane of the waveguide and accommodated in a specially designed metal block for measurement. This technique is sufficiently flexible and repeatable so as to permit complex 3-D waveguide components with low loss and excellent surface finish to be realised at low cost. Various rectangular waveguide sections with operating frequencies from 110 to 320 GHz have been fabricated and measured to evaluate this approach.

articleTitle: A fully integrated high efficiency SiGe HBT class F power amplifier at 2.2 GHz
publicationTitle: 2003 High Frequency Postgraduate Student Colloquium (Cat. No.03TH8707)
abstract: This paper presents a fully integrated high efficiency SiGe HBT class F power amplifier (PA). A maximum on-chip power added efficiency (PAE) of 25 % has been measured, which at 2.2 GHz and a supply voltage of 1.3 V, is to the forefront of fully integrated HBT class F power amplifier design. The PA is suitable for applications that include DECT and GSM which employ the constant envelope modulation scheme, GMSK. The power amplifier was fabricated using an advanced 0.18 um BiCMOS process [J. Kirchgessner et al., September 2001].

articleTitle: Dielectric characterization using the microstrip resonator method
publicationTitle: 2003 High Frequency Postgraduate Student Colloquium (Cat. No.03TH8707)
abstract: Microstrip ring resonators and end coupled resonators with different substrate width, feed line length and gap width are fabricated and the /spl epsi//sub eff/ is measured. It is shown that these parameters can critically affect measurement results. A substrate width of twice the resonator diameter for the sample is recommended for correct measurement of /spl epsi//sub r/. The effect of the coupling gap between the feed line and the resonator is investigated where too small a gap can induce a change of resonant frequency resulting in a measurement error for /spl epsi//sub eff/ extraction. A suitable gap is recommended for each type of substrate under examination.

articleTitle: Characterisation of body-shadowing effects in the indoor environment at 5.2 GHz
publicationTitle: 2003 High Frequency Postgraduate Student Colloquium (Cat. No.03TH8707)
abstract: Human body shadowing effects can considerably influence the channel characteristics of indoor radio communication systems. In this work, body-shadowing effects were measured for a line-of-sight (LOS) point-to-point 5.2 GHz link with up to 3 pedestrians moving within a 42 m/sup 2/ room. The results show that received power values are significantly dependent on whether or not the user's body obstructed the direct ray to the transmitter. Under obstructed conditions, the measured body shadowing effect was an attenuation of up to 10 dB. The first order statistics for the experimental scenarios tend to be Rice distributed with the K factor decreasing as the number of pedestrians present increased.

articleTitle: Outage probability comparison of distributed antenna diversity and single site antenna diversity
publicationTitle: 2003 High Frequency Postgraduate Student Colloquium (Cat. No.03TH8707)
abstract: In highly built-up urban areas, where shadowing is a severe problem, distributed antenna diversity represents a more effective fade mitigation scheme than conventional single site antenna diversity. It integrates the advantage of both micro and macro antenna diversities. In this contribution, a hybrid model using Gaussian fast fading and ray tracing is used to obtain the unconditional outage probability and the performance of the distributed antenna and single site antenna structures are compared. For the distributed antenna a comparison between coherent combining diversity and selection diversity schemes has also been made.

articleTitle: The effect of the gate Schottky diode on pHEMT power amplifier performance
publicationTitle: 2003 High Frequency Postgraduate Student Colloquium (Cat. No.03TH8707)
abstract: This paper presents for the first time a practical systematic investigation into the effects of gate Schottky parameter values on large-signal amplifier performance. The use of a new Schottky diode model for a packaged pHEMT device shows significant improvements over the vendor supplied model when used in the non-linear characterisation of a class A power amplifier. Special emphasis is placed on the effect these values exhibit on the ability of the large-signal model to predict measured power amplifier characteristics including gain, output power, efficiency, linearity, ACPR and non-linear spectral regrowth.

articleTitle: Design of wideband superconducting coplanar delay lines
publicationTitle: 2003 High Frequency Postgraduate Student Colloquium (Cat. No.03TH8707)
abstract: A novel superconducting delay line is presented, it is formed from a coplanar transmission line, the transmission line has a meander structure, which is then curled into a double spiral to maximise the use of the substrate area. Full-wave simulations are conducted on a 0.5 m coplanar line of this type and also a conventional double-spiral line for comparison. Geometric factors limiting the achievable bandwidth are addressed. To extract the device delay and loss without incurring the problems of the input and output connections, AC coupled measurements are done using a 25 ns delay line as a resonator. Quality factors of the resonances from 20 MHz to 20 GHz are measured. The estimated group delay of the delay line is given.

articleTitle: Stepwise refinement algorithms for prediction of user location using receive signal strength indication in infrastructure WLANs
publicationTitle: 2003 High Frequency Postgraduate Student Colloquium (Cat. No.03TH8707)
abstract: This paper examines several algorithms for improving the estimation of user location using received strength signal indication (RSSI) values in a standard infrastructure wireless local area network (WLAN). The basic method of estimating a mobile user's position is the variation of RSSl with transmitter/receiver separation. Unfortunately, due to both external interference and the inherent uncertainty present in RSSI measurements, this approach leads to unacceptable errors in the position estimates. In order to improve the overall accuracy of the system, several refinement algorithms have been examined and simulated to investigate their effect on the system accuracy, with the results presented herein.

articleTitle: The comparison and combination of CMOS inductor Q-enhancement techniques
publicationTitle: 2003 High Frequency Postgraduate Student Colloquium (Cat. No.03TH8707)
abstract: Much emphasis and blame has been placed on integrated silicon inductors and their poor Q values, leading to degradation in circuit performance, especially at RF and microwave frequencies. This is no more evident than in WLAN applications at 5.25 GHz where poor Q values can induce increased noise figure, power consumption and linearity deterioration. This paper will present a concise comparison of non-invasive Q-enhancement techniques using patterned ground shields, stacked metal, thick copper and differential inductors. A differential stacked metal inductor with patterned ground shield will also be demonstrated for its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Performance of a broadband ring element reflectarray
publicationTitle: 2003 High Frequency Postgraduate Student Colloquium (Cat. No.03TH8707)
abstract: The scattering from a grounded array of double layer ring and concentric ring elements is compared at X-band. For both periodic arrays, it is shown that the reflection phase variation with ring diameter is controlled by the difference in the centre resonant frequency of the two elements. This parameter can be selected to give a linear phase versus ring size plot with a small gradient which is required for broadband reflectarray antenna design applications. The TLM method was used as a computer simulation tool and the results were compared with waveguide simulator measurements to demonstrate the validity of the predictions.

articleTitle: Total body water content observations using cavity - perturbation techniques
publicationTitle: 2003 High Frequency Postgraduate Student Colloquium (Cat. No.03TH8707)
abstract: A novel technique for determining the total body water (TBW) of patients suffering with abnormal hydration, using resonant perturbation methods, has been proposed. The dielectric properties of the body are determined by placing a volunteer in a large cavity resonator and measuring the subsequent change in its resonant frequency, f/sub res/, and quality factor, Q. Utilising the relationship that moisture content correlates to these dielectric properties, it is shown that the measured response of these parameters enable the determination of whole body water content.

articleTitle: Performance of 4-ary ASK for optical communication systems in dispersive, nonlinear environments
publicationTitle: 2003 High Frequency Postgraduate Student Colloquium (Cat. No.03TH8707)
abstract: Multi-level modulations schemes for optical communication systems use less bandwidth for a given data rate, and so besides having potential spectral efficiency advantages, may also provide reduced sensitivity to fiber dispersion and nonlinearities. In this paper we model the propagation of 4-level amplitude shift keying signals, and compare their performance, for both return-to-zero and non-return-to-zero formats, to on-off keying. At the cost of a back-to-back sensitivity penalty, significantly increased dispersion reach is shown, and reduced impact of nonlinearities is also demonstrated in a multi-channel environment.

articleTitle: Investigations into the performance of various HBV physical structures for high efficiency harmonic generation
publicationTitle: 2003 High Frequency Postgraduate Student Colloquium (Cat. No.03TH8707)
abstract: Heterostructure barrier varactors (HBV) with different physical structures have been investigated and characterised for their capacitance-voltage characteristic and device series resistance. This is a novel concept to increase the HBV capacitance modulation whilst minimize the device series resistance for the NLTL in achieving optimum harmonic generation. Various capacitance modulation characteristics can be engineered by shaping the HBV mesa with either an undercut or side slope on the mesa body without the need to modify the original epilayer properties. This concept greatly improves the quality of the NLTL and essential for broadband harmonic generation which required large amount of NLTL sections for optimum conversion.

articleTitle: Microstrip-fed rectangular dielectric resonator antenna
publicationTitle: 2003 High Frequency Postgraduate Student Colloquium (Cat. No.03TH8707)
abstract: The wireless LAN (WLAN) revolution is about to sweep the globe. WLAN access points are being set up all over the world. The need to design an antenna with greater efficiency and wider bandwidth is essential for high-speed wireless data transfer. This paper describes the numerical study of microstrip-coupled rectangular DRA (RDRA) using a commercial E.M. simulator. The RDRA is positioned on top of an open-end microstrip feed line and hence coupled to the microstrip line electromagnetically. The dominant TE/sub 111//sup y/ mode is excited in the frequency range of 2.20-2.95 GHz. The study includes several substrate configurations. The results on the effect of the position of RDRA with respect to the strip line and substrate parameters on the frequency and impedance bandwidth are reported.

articleTitle: Mutual coupling effects between coplanar crossed skew dipoles
publicationTitle: 2003 High Frequency Postgraduate Student Colloquium (Cat. No.03TH8707)
abstract: In this paper mutual coupling effects between coplanar crossed skew dipoles have been investigated both experimentally and theoretically. The crosspolarisation, resonant frequency, bandwidth and mutual impedance are shown to vary with the angle between the dipoles and their relative length. A new approach has been used to calculate the mutual impedance from the measured or simulated value of the driving point impedance of the coupled crossed dipoles and the self-impedance of the individual elements. The results from the computer model have been compared with measurements and are shown to be in good agreement.

articleTitle: Multi-layer ceramic capacitor (MLCC) termination height - effect on electrical performance
publicationTitle: 2003 High Frequency Postgraduate Student Colloquium (Cat. No.03TH8707)
abstract: This paper investigates the influence of metal termination height (H) on a multi-layer ceramic capacitor and its overall electrical response. Since the path to the active layers of the capacitor is via a block of highly conductive metal, it is of interest to determine the effect this has on the capacitors' overall performance. A mixture of theory, simulation, and measurement are used to validate and refine the individual component parameter of inductance per unit height for commercial MLCCs in the frequency range up to 10 GHz.

articleTitle: Six-port QPSK receiver
publicationTitle: 2003 High Frequency Postgraduate Student Colloquium (Cat. No.03TH8707)
abstract: The operation of a six-port QPSK receiver design is described in this paper. The device consists of two inputs and four outputs. The inputs are the RF and local oscillator (LO) signals while the outputs are the four demodulated QPSK signals. The phase of each individual output signal is located in a different quadrant. The theory for the circuit is described here.

articleTitle: Modelling of Rayleigh backscattering in plastic optical fiber
publicationTitle: 2003 High Frequency Postgraduate Student Colloquium (Cat. No.03TH8707)
abstract: The Rayleigh scattering coefficient within plastic optical fiber (POF), which is also called turbidity, has been investigated and parameters affecting the level of turbidity have been located and discussed. The Rayleigh attenuation model has been built on turbidity and has been verified by comparing with published data. Disparities between the model and published data have been discussed. The Rayleigh backscattering model based on turbidity and fractional recapture coefficient within the fiber has been built and the dependence of the total backscattered optical power on wavelength has been discussed.

articleTitle: On establishing a calibration and comparison framework for RF and microwave HPA linearisers
publicationTitle: 2003 High Frequency Postgraduate Student Colloquium (Cat. No.03TH8707)
abstract: Performance calibration of lineariser schemes designed to offset the impairments arising through high power amplifier (HPA) nonlinearities is addressed in this paper. Relating to the importance of linearisation in future reconfigurable ultra wideband (UW) mobile wireless communication systems, the benefits of the percentage linearisation area (PLA) measure is illustrated through EVM calculations ('simulation measurements') of an appropriate test signal after its passage through a typical HPA without linearisation and with varying degrees of linearisation.

articleTitle: Interaction of emerging mobile telecommunication systems with the human body
publicationTitle: 2003 High Frequency Postgraduate Student Colloquium (Cat. No.03TH8707)
abstract: Emerging telecommunication systems, with new devices and new transmission techniques modify the exposure of the population to electromagnetic fields [UMTS Forum, October 2000] [UMTS Forum, January 2002]. Although the risk for human health is currently thought to be low, there is a need to clarify these changes. This work involves analyzing typical scenarios and worst cases and developing new techniques and standards for the compliance testing of personal communication devices. The approach can be divided into two interconnected parallel strands. Numerical models have been developed, tested and refined to reproduce and predict non-ionizing radiation (NIR) exposure of the human body using finite difference time domain technique (FDTD). Experimental validation has been performed, using physical phantoms and human volunteers.

articleTitle: Microwave based wheat grain kernel characterisation
publicationTitle: 2003 High Frequency Postgraduate Student Colloquium (Cat. No.03TH8707)
abstract: A low-cost microwave source and detector is designed to drive a microwave cylindrical cavity to determine the wet mass and moisture content of single wheat grain kernels. Differences in wet mass and moisture content can be distinguished from the changes in resonant frequency and attenuation. Moisture content (8% to 16%) of single wheat grain kernels was measured. Experimental results are presented and the calibration equations are implemented in a microcontroller. Wet mass and moisture content are shown on an LCD display on the microcontroller. The measurement procedure and evaluation of the system are presented in the proposed paper.

articleTitle: Intermodulation distortion characteristics of RF MOSFETs
publicationTitle: 2003 High Frequency Postgraduate Student Colloquium (Cat. No.03TH8707)
abstract: Intermodulation distortion (IMD) prediction capabilities of a recently developed MOSFET model are assessed by analysing the first to fifth order derivatives of the model, extracted from DC and small-signal s-parameter data. The computed main characteristics and the associated derivatives are shown to be continuous over the entire bias plane, including below threshold. Results of two-tone tests for the case of a MOSFET process are presented. Weak-signal, third and fifth intermodulation distortion products are successfully correlated with the derivatives of the model for a range of bias points, and this analysis is extended to more realistic WCDMA signals.

articleTitle: Investigation on properties of left-handed materials
publicationTitle: 2003 High Frequency Postgraduate Student Colloquium (Cat. No.03TH8707)
abstract: This paper describes some of the unique properties which materials with negative real parts of electric permittivity and magnetic permeability have to offer when interfaced with materials of positive parameters. It explains the boundary conditions which exist in such cases and the resulting equations which characterise the propagation in each medium. It also demonstrates how the electric field and magnetic field form the right three triplets in a positive medium and the left three triplets in a negative region. Further a model has been built to characterise the wave propagation through the structure using the boundary conditions derived.

articleTitle: Efficient simulation of interconnects in high-speed circuits
publicationTitle: 2003 High Frequency Postgraduate Student Colloquium (Cat. No.03TH8707)
abstract: The paper presents an efficient approach for the simulation of interconnects in high-speed circuits based on measured data or simulated EM data. The approach involves forming an initial transmission-line model based on a resonant approach introduced by the authors and subsequently tuning this model to match the measured data. Following tuning, the model is converted to a state-space formulation. This then enables a standard model reduction routine such as the Lanczos process to be applied so as to gain further improvements from a computational efficiency viewpoint. The overall result is a highly efficient interconnect model based on measured data.

articleTitle: 2003 High Frequency Postgraduate Student Colloquium (Cat. No.03TH8707)
publicationTitle: 2003 High Frequency Postgraduate Student Colloquium (Cat. No.03TH8707)
abstract: The following topics are dealt with: wave propagation, dielectric characterisation, nonlinear devices, guided propagation, passive devices, antennas, wireless LAN, nonlinear transmission lines, capacitors, phased lock loop and QPSK detector.

articleTitle: A compact InGaP/GaAs DHBT model based on symbolically defined device in ADS for microwave applications
publicationTitle: 2003 High Frequency Postgraduate Student Colloquium (Cat. No.03TH8707)
abstract: In this paper a compact double heterojunction bipolar transistor (DHBT) large signal model together with the related parameter extraction and development methodology is presented. The model is developed using the non-linear symbolically defined device (SDD) in HP ADS. The model, which is valid for small and large signal simulations, is discussed and validated for wide range of biases, signal frequencies and device temperatures.

articleTitle: Dispersive FDTD modeling on near field imaging in multi-layer left-handed meta-materials at microwave frequencies
publicationTitle: 2003 High Frequency Postgraduate Student Colloquium (Cat. No.03TH8707)
abstract: 'Perfect' imaging in left-handed meta-materials (LHMs) is constrained by surface wave losses in near field. A multi-layer LHMs structure can be deployed to reduce the losses particularly in near field imaging. Furthermore, we demonstrate how to use a multiple-layer LHMs structure with variable gap distance to enhance near field image over large stack thickness in near field imaging at microwave frequencies. The theoretical prediction is verified with good agreement using a causal two-dimensional dispersive FDTD simulation.

articleTitle: Investigation of the spectral advantages of sol-gel layered erbium doped waveguide amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2003 High Frequency Postgraduate Student Colloquium (Cat. No.03TH8707)
abstract: High levels of net gain have recently been reported in sol-gel phosphorous-aluminium co-doped silica waveguides. However, compositions providing both high net gain and large spectral width have not yet been achieved. In this paper we propose the use of laminated cores of multiple compositions to achieve improved spectral performance in erbium-doped waveguide amplifiers. We demonstrate the potential advantages of this technique by simulations of cores laminated from previously demonstrated individual glasses.

articleTitle: Characterisation of negative meta materials based on generalised periodic structure concept
publicationTitle: 2003 High Frequency Postgraduate Student Colloquium (Cat. No.03TH8707)
abstract: In this paper we studied the negative refractive index in electromagnetic periodic structures and it is shown how negative refraction can be identified from the dispersion behaviour of periodic structures, which is obtained by considering entire periodic structure as a block. The effect of spatial harmonics towards negative refraction is also presented which is neglected in past analysis.

articleTitle: Modified planar inverted-L antenna
publicationTitle: 2003 High Frequency Postgraduate Student Colloquium (Cat. No.03TH8707)
abstract: A hybrid inverted-L antenna (HIL) has been shown to reduce the physical height of a square planar monopole antenna, while retaining a relatively wide impedance bandwidth and good radiation pattern characteristics. The introduction of horizontal slots in the vertical edges of the antenna cause the surface current to meander, resulting in a decrease in the lower edge frequency of the impedance bandwidth. The impact of different sizes and arrangements of slots on impedance and radiation pattern bandwidth, gain and surface current distribution is simulated using transmission line modelling (TLM). Simulated results for impedance bandwidth are verified with measurements. With other modifications these antennas are proposed for wireless and mobile applications in the 2.45 GHz and 5.8 GHz ISM bands.

articleTitle: Pulse compression using non-linear transmission lines (NLTLs) based on Schottky quantum barrier varactor diodes
publicationTitle: 2003 High Frequency Postgraduate Student Colloquium (Cat. No.03TH8707)
abstract: Improving the bandwidth of multilayer PCB line cards in a telecommunications system is reported in this paper. The signal distortion due to frequency dependent attenuation and dispersion is compensated by regenerating the high frequency components of digital pulses using shock wave generation within the NLTL. Operation of the NLTL using conventional Schottky diode technology and using Schottky quantum barrier varactor (SQBV) diodes is discussed and compared.

articleTitle: Microwave phase-locked loop circuit development and efficiency improvement
publicationTitle: 2003 High Frequency Postgraduate Student Colloquium (Cat. No.03TH8707)
abstract: A sampling phase detector (SPD) circuit for locking a microwave VCO, at 19.6 GHz, is proposed. Based on the step recovery diode as the locking source and the Schottky diode mixer, the SPD is implemented into the phase-locked loop (PLL) concept. Harmonic balance simulation is used to determine the output power level. Different drive levels are examined within the PLL circuit to achieve the lowest power level for a reliable lock and hence the optimum input/output match is determined for best efficiency.

articleTitle: Investigation into aircraft air vent geometry and its effect on electromagnetic radiation
publicationTitle: 2003 High Frequency Postgraduate Student Colloquium (Cat. No.03TH8707)
abstract: An air vent mounted on the side of a jet engine nacelle provides cooling for on-board electronics. This paper investigates the geometry of the air vent and predicts the effect the geometry has on incident electromagnetic radiation. Simulations using 3D-TLM were performed to provide power density plots at 3 GHz and 8 GHz for two bounding areas of incident radiation. The field plots were used to predict how radiation was entering the vent. The return loss of the vent has also been calculated for the two bounding areas.
